docs.title: Customer Support System
docs.text: A lightweight MVP for a GenAI-powered customer support workflow using FastAPI, Celery, PostgreSQL, Redis, and a local LLM (Ollama).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Event-driven workflow: Analyze → Classify → Generate Response
  • Local LLM via Ollama (llama3.1:8b)
  • Simple persistence for tickets and results
  • API-first with background processing

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Ticket submission API
  • Celery-based async processing
  • Prompt templating via Jinja2
  • Typed schemas with Pydantic v2

docs.title: Links
docs.text:
• API Docs: /docs
  • Health: /healthz, /readyz

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
• Install Ollama and pull a model: ollama pull llama3.1:8b
  • Start API and Worker:
  • DATABASE_PASSWORD=customer_support_password ./scripts/start_api.sh
  • DATABASE_PASSWORD=customer_support_password ./scripts/start_worker.sh
  • Open the UI: http://localhost:8080/ui

docs.title: Production
docs.text: See Deployment → Production for environment variables, reverse proxy, hardening, and a deployment checklist.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
• GET /healthz → ok
  • GET /readyz → ready

docs.title: Support Tickets
docs.text:
• POST /support/tickets
  • body: SupportTicketSchema
  • returns: 202 Accepted with ticket_id, task_id
  • GET /support/tickets
  • query: limit, offset, status, customer_email
  • returns: list of tickets (filtered if query provided)
  • GET /support/tickets/{ticket_id}
  • returns: ticket details
  • POST /support/tickets/{ticket_id}/retry
  • re-queue a failed ticket for processing; 202 on success

Schema for incoming customer support tickets.

This schema defines the structure for customer support tickets in the lightweight MVP. It includes only essential fields needed for basic ticket processing and AI response generation.

Source code in app/schemas/customer_support_schema.py 
class SupportTicketSchema(BaseModel):
    """Schema for incoming customer support tickets.

    This schema defines the structure for customer support tickets
    in the lightweight MVP. It includes only essential fields needed
    for basic ticket processing and AI response generation.
    """

    id: str = Field(..., description="Unique ticket identifier")
    customer_email: str = Field(..., description="Customer email address")
    subject: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=200, description="Ticket subject line")
    content: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=2000, description="Detailed ticket content")
    priority: Optional[str] = Field(default="medium", description="Ticket priority level")
    created_at: Optional[datetime] = Field(
        default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        description="Ticket creation timestamp",
    )

    model_config = ConfigDict(
        json_schema_extra={
            "example": {
                "id": "ticket_12345",
                "customer_email": "customer@example.com",
                "subject": "Login issues with my account",
                "content": "I'm unable to log into my account. I keep getting an error message saying 'Invalid credentials' even though I'm sure my password is correct.",
                "priority": "high",
            }
        }
    )

docs.title: app.workflows.customer_support_workflow.CustomerSupportWorkflow
docs.text:
Bases: Workflow

Customer support ticket processing workflow.

This workflow processes incoming customer support tickets through a series of AI-powered analysis and response generation steps:

  1. AnalyzeTicketNode: Analyzes ticket content for classification and sentiment
  2. ClassifyTicketNode: Validates and enhances classification results
  3. GenerateResponseNode: Generates appropriate response based on classification

The workflow follows the lightweight MVP pattern with 3 nodes maximum and simple, linear processing flow.

Source code in app/workflows/customer_support_workflow.py 
class CustomerSupportWorkflow(Workflow):
    """Customer support ticket processing workflow.

    This workflow processes incoming customer support tickets through
    a series of AI-powered analysis and response generation steps:

    1. AnalyzeTicketNode: Analyzes ticket content for classification and sentiment
    2. ClassifyTicketNode: Validates and enhances classification results
    3. GenerateResponseNode: Generates appropriate response based on classification

    The workflow follows the lightweight MVP pattern with 3 nodes maximum
    and simple, linear processing flow.
    """

    workflow_schema = WorkflowSchema(
        description="Customer support ticket processing workflow for lightweight MVP",
        event_schema=SupportTicketSchema,
        start=AnalyzeTicketNode,
        nodes=[
            NodeConfig(
                node=AnalyzeTicketNode,
                connections=[ClassifyTicketNode],
                description="Analyzes incoming support tickets for classification and sentiment using Ollama"
            ),
            NodeConfig(
                node=ClassifyTicketNode,
                connections=[GenerateResponseNode],
                description="Validates and enhances classification results with business logic"
            ),
            NodeConfig(
                node=GenerateResponseNode,
                connections=[],
                description="Generates helpful responses based on classification using Ollama"
            ),
        ],
    )

docs.title: app.workflows.customer_support_nodes.analyze_ticket_node.AnalyzeTicketNode
docs.text:
Bases: Node

Analyzes incoming support tickets for classification and sentiment.

This node processes customer support tickets to extract key information such as intent classification, sentiment analysis, and priority scoring. It uses Ollama with Llama 3.1 8B for lightweight, local AI processing.

Source code in app/workflows/customer_support_nodes/analyze_ticket_node.py 
class AnalyzeTicketNode(Node):
    """Analyzes incoming support tickets for classification and sentiment.

    This node processes customer support tickets to extract key information
    such as intent classification, sentiment analysis, and priority scoring.
    It uses Ollama with Llama 3.1 8B for lightweight, local AI processing.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.ollama_url = f"{settings.ollama_base_url}/api/generate"
        self.model = settings.ollama_model
        self.start_time = None

    def process(self, task_context: TaskContext) -> TaskContext:
        """Process the ticket analysis workflow.

        Args:
            task_context: The task context containing the ticket data

        Returns:
            Updated TaskContext with analysis results

        Raises:
            OllamaConnectionError: If unable to connect to Ollama service
            InvalidTicketDataError: If ticket data is malformed
        """
        self.start_time = time.time()
        ticket = task_context.event

        logger.info(f"Starting ticket analysis", extra={
            "ticket_id": ticket.id,
            "node": self.node_name,
            "status": "started"
        })

        try:
            # Build the prompt using the template
            prompt = self._build_analysis_prompt(ticket)

            # Call Ollama API
            classification_result = self._call_ollama(prompt)

            # Parse the JSON response
            classification_data = self._parse_ollama_response(classification_result)

            # Calculate processing time
            processing_time = time.time() - self.start_time

            # Store results in task context
            task_context.nodes[self.node_name] = {
                "status": "completed",
                "classification": classification_data,
                "processing_time": processing_time,
                "model_used": self.model
            }

            logger.info(f"Ticket analysis completed", extra={
                "ticket_id": ticket.id,
                "node": self.node_name,
                "status": "completed",
                "processing_time": processing_time,
                "category": classification_data.get("category"),
                "sentiment": classification_data.get("sentiment")
            })

        except Exception as e:
            processing_time = time.time() - self.start_time if self.start_time else 0

            logger.error(f"Ticket analysis failed", extra={
                "ticket_id": ticket.id,
                "node": self.node_name,
                "status": "error",
                "error": str(e),
                "processing_time": processing_time
            })

            task_context.nodes[self.node_name] = {
                "status": "error",
                "error": str(e),
                "processing_time": processing_time
            }

        return task_context

    def _build_analysis_prompt(self, ticket) -> str:
        """Build the analysis prompt using the Jinja2 template.

        Args:
            ticket: The support ticket data

        Returns:
            Formatted prompt string
        """
        try:
            return PromptManager.get_prompt(
                "ticket_analysis",
                ticket=ticket
            )
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to build analysis prompt: {str(e)}")
            # Fallback to simple prompt
            return f"""
            Analyze this support ticket:
            Subject: {ticket.subject}
            Content: {ticket.content}
            Priority: {ticket.priority}

            Provide classification in JSON format:
            {{
              "category": "technical",
              "sentiment": "negative",
              "urgency": "high",
              "confidence": 0.85,
              "reasoning": "Brief explanation"
            }}
            """

    def _call_ollama(self, prompt: str) -> str:
        """Call Ollama API for ticket analysis.

        Args:
            prompt: The formatted prompt to send to Ollama

        Returns:
            Raw response from Ollama

        Raises:
            requests.RequestException: If API call fails
        """
        backoffs = [2, 4, 8]
        last_err: Exception | None = None
        for attempt, delay in enumerate([0] + backoffs, start=1):
            try:
                response = requests.post(
                    self.ollama_url,
                    json={
                        "model": self.model,
                        "prompt": prompt,
                        "stream": False,
                        "options": {
                            "temperature": 0.1,
                            "top_p": 0.9,
                        },
                    },
                    timeout=60 if attempt == 1 else 30,
                )
                if response.status_code != 200:
                    raise requests.RequestException(
                        f"Ollama API returned status {response.status_code}: {response.text}"
                    )
                result = response.json()
                return result.get("response", "")
            except requests.RequestException as e:
                last_err = e
                logger.error(f"Ollama API call failed (attempt {attempt}): {str(e)}")
                if delay:
                    try:
                        import time as _t
                        _t.sleep(delay)
                    except Exception:
                        pass
        # All attempts failed
        assert last_err is not None
        raise last_err

    def _parse_ollama_response(self, response: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Parse the JSON response from Ollama.

        Args:
            response: Raw response string from Ollama

        Returns:
            Parsed classification data

        Raises:
            ValueError: If response cannot be parsed as JSON
        """
        try:
            # Try to extract JSON from the response
            # Sometimes LLMs include markdown formatting
            if "```json" in response:
                # Extract JSON from markdown code block
                start = response.find("```json") + 7
                end = response.find("```", start)
                json_str = response[start:end].strip()
            elif "```" in response:
                # Extract JSON from code block
                start = response.find("```") + 3
                end = response.find("```", start)
                json_str = response[start:end].strip()
            else:
                # Try to find JSON in the response
                json_str = response.strip()

            # Parse the JSON
            data = json.loads(json_str)

            # Validate required fields
            required_fields = ["category", "sentiment", "urgency", "confidence"]
            for field in required_fields:
                if field not in data:
                    raise ValueError(f"Missing required field: {field}")

            return data

        except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to parse Ollama response: {str(e)}")
            logger.error(f"Raw response: {response}")

            # Return default classification on parsing failure
            return {
                "category": "general",
                "sentiment": "neutral",
                "urgency": "medium",
                "confidence": 0.5,
                "reasoning": "Default classification due to parsing error"
            }

Bases: Node

Processes and validates ticket classification results.

This node takes the raw analysis results from AnalyzeTicketNode and converts them into structured classification data. It also applies business logic for classification validation and enhancement.

Source code in app/workflows/customer_support_nodes/classify_ticket_node.py 
class ClassifyTicketNode(Node):
    """Processes and validates ticket classification results.

    This node takes the raw analysis results from AnalyzeTicketNode
    and converts them into structured classification data. It also
    applies business logic for classification validation and enhancement.
    """

    def process(self, task_context: TaskContext) -> TaskContext:
        """Process the ticket classification workflow.

        Args:
            task_context: The task context containing analysis results

        Returns:
            Updated TaskContext with validated classification
        """
        ticket = task_context.event

        logger.info(f"Starting ticket classification", extra={
            "ticket_id": ticket.id,
            "node": self.node_name,
            "status": "started"
        })

        try:
            # Get analysis results from previous node
            analysis_node = task_context.nodes.get("AnalyzeTicketNode", {})

            if analysis_node.get("status") != "completed":
                raise ValueError("Analysis node did not complete successfully")

            # Extract classification data
            raw_classification = analysis_node.get("classification", {})

            # Validate and enhance classification
            classification_data = self._validate_classification(raw_classification)

            # Apply business logic for classification enhancement
            enhanced_classification = self._enhance_classification(
                classification_data, ticket
            )

            # Store results in task context
            task_context.nodes[self.node_name] = {
                "status": "completed",
                "classification": enhanced_classification,
                "original_analysis": raw_classification
            }

            logger.info(f"Ticket classification completed", extra={
                "ticket_id": ticket.id,
                "node": self.node_name,
                "status": "completed",
                "category": enhanced_classification.category,
                "sentiment": enhanced_classification.sentiment,
                "urgency": enhanced_classification.urgency
            })

        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Ticket classification failed", extra={
                "ticket_id": ticket.id,
                "node": self.node_name,
                "status": "error",
                "error": str(e)
            })

            task_context.nodes[self.node_name] = {
                "status": "error",
                "error": str(e)
            }

        return task_context

    def _validate_classification(self, raw_data: Dict[str, Any]) -> SimpleClassificationSchema:
        """Validate and convert raw classification data to structured format.

        Args:
            raw_data: Raw classification data from AI analysis

        Returns:
            Validated SimpleClassificationSchema object
        """
        # Validate category
        category = raw_data.get("category", "general").lower()
        valid_categories = [
            "technical", "billing", "general", "feature_request", 
            "bug_report", "account", "security"
        ]
        if category not in valid_categories:
            category = "general"

        # Validate sentiment
        sentiment = raw_data.get("sentiment", "neutral").lower()
        valid_sentiments = ["positive", "neutral", "negative"]
        if sentiment not in valid_sentiments:
            sentiment = "neutral"

        # Validate urgency
        urgency = raw_data.get("urgency", "medium").lower()
        valid_urgency_levels = ["low", "medium", "high"]
        if urgency not in valid_urgency_levels:
            urgency = "medium"

        # Validate confidence
        confidence = raw_data.get("confidence", 0.5)
        if not isinstance(confidence, (int, float)) or confidence < 0 or confidence > 1:
            confidence = 0.5

        return SimpleClassificationSchema(
            category=category,
            sentiment=sentiment,
            urgency=urgency,
            confidence=confidence
        )

    def _enhance_classification(
        self, 
        classification: SimpleClassificationSchema, 
        ticket
    ) -> SimpleClassificationSchema:
        """Apply business logic to enhance classification.

        Args:
            classification: Validated classification data
            ticket: Original ticket data

        Returns:
            Enhanced classification with business logic applied
        """
        # Adjust urgency based on ticket priority
        if ticket.priority == "high" and classification.urgency == "low":
            classification.urgency = "medium"
        elif ticket.priority == "low" and classification.urgency == "high":
            classification.urgency = "medium"

        # Adjust sentiment based on urgency
        if classification.urgency == "high" and classification.sentiment == "positive":
            # High urgency with positive sentiment might indicate sarcasm or frustration
            classification.sentiment = "negative"

        # Adjust confidence based on content length
        if len(ticket.content) < 50:
            # Short content might have lower confidence
            classification.confidence = min(classification.confidence, 0.7)

        return classification

class GenerateResponseNode(Node):
    """Generates helpful responses for customer support tickets.

    This node uses the classification results to generate appropriate,
    helpful responses for customer support tickets. It uses Ollama with
    Llama 3.1 8B for lightweight, local AI response generation.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.ollama_url = f"{settings.ollama_base_url}/api/generate"
        self.model = settings.ollama_model
        self.start_time = None

    def process(self, task_context: TaskContext) -> TaskContext:
        """Process the response generation workflow.

        Args:
            task_context: The task context containing ticket and classification data

        Returns:
            Updated TaskContext with generated response
        """
        self.start_time = time.time()
        ticket = task_context.event

        logger.info(f"Starting response generation", extra={
            "ticket_id": ticket.id,
            "node": self.node_name,
            "status": "started"
        })

        try:
            # Get classification from previous node
            classification_node = task_context.nodes.get("ClassifyTicketNode", {})

            if classification_node.get("status") != "completed":
                raise ValueError("Classification node did not complete successfully")

            classification = classification_node.get("classification")

            # Build the response prompt using the template
            prompt = self._build_response_prompt(ticket, classification)

            # Call Ollama API
            response_result = self._call_ollama(prompt)

            # Parse the JSON response
            response_data = self._parse_ollama_response(response_result)

            # Calculate processing time
            processing_time = time.time() - self.start_time

            # Store results in task context
            task_context.nodes[self.node_name] = {
                "status": "completed",
                "response": response_data,
                "processing_time": processing_time,
                "model_used": self.model
            }

            logger.info(f"Response generation completed", extra={
                "ticket_id": ticket.id,
                "node": self.node_name,
                "status": "completed",
                "processing_time": processing_time,
                "response_type": response_data.response_type
            })

        except Exception as e:
            processing_time = time.time() - self.start_time if self.start_time else 0

            logger.error(f"Response generation failed", extra={
                "ticket_id": ticket.id,
                "node": self.node_name,
                "status": "error",
                "error": str(e),
                "processing_time": processing_time
            })

            task_context.nodes[self.node_name] = {
                "status": "error",
                "error": str(e),
                "processing_time": processing_time
            }

        return task_context

    def _build_response_prompt(self, ticket, classification) -> str:
        """Build the response generation prompt using the Jinja2 template.

        Args:
            ticket: The support ticket data
            classification: The classification results

        Returns:
            Formatted prompt string
        """
        try:
            return PromptManager.get_prompt(
                "response_generation",
                ticket=ticket,
                classification=classification
            )
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to build response prompt: {str(e)}")
            # Fallback to simple prompt
            return f"""
            Generate a helpful response for this support ticket:

            Subject: {ticket.subject}
            Content: {ticket.content}
            Priority: {ticket.priority}
            Category: {classification.category}
            Sentiment: {classification.sentiment}
            Urgency: {classification.urgency}

            Provide response in JSON format:
            {{
              "response_text": "Your helpful response here...",
              "response_type": "automated",
              "suggested_actions": ["action1", "action2"],
              "confidence": 0.9
            }}
            """

    def _call_ollama(self, prompt: str) -> str:
        """Call Ollama API for response generation.

        Args:
            prompt: The formatted prompt to send to Ollama

        Returns:
            Raw response from Ollama

        Raises:
            requests.RequestException: If API call fails
        """
        backoffs = [2, 4, 8]
        last_err: Exception | None = None
        for attempt, delay in enumerate([0] + backoffs, start=1):
            try:
                response = requests.post(
                    self.ollama_url,
                    json={
                        "model": self.model,
                        "prompt": prompt,
                        "stream": False,
                        "options": {
                            "temperature": 0.3,
                            "top_p": 0.9,
                        },
                    },
                    timeout=60 if attempt == 1 else 30,
                )
                if response.status_code != 200:
                    raise requests.RequestException(
                        f"Ollama API returned status {response.status_code}: {response.text}"
                    )
                result = response.json()
                return result.get("response", "")
            except requests.RequestException as e:
                last_err = e
                logger.error(f"Ollama API call failed (attempt {attempt}): {str(e)}")
                if delay:
                    try:
                        import time as _t
                        _t.sleep(delay)
                    except Exception:
                        pass
        assert last_err is not None
        raise last_err

    def _parse_ollama_response(self, response: str) -> ResponseSchema:
        """Parse the JSON response from Ollama.

        Args:
            response: Raw response string from Ollama

        Returns:
            Parsed ResponseSchema object

        Raises:
            ValueError: If response cannot be parsed as JSON
        """
        try:
            # Try to extract JSON from the response
            if "```json" in response:
                # Extract JSON from markdown code block
                start = response.find("```json") + 7
                end = response.find("```", start)
                json_str = response[start:end].strip()
            elif "```" in response:
                # Extract JSON from code block
                start = response.find("```") + 3
                end = response.find("```", start)
                json_str = response[start:end].strip()
            else:
                # Try to find JSON in the response
                json_str = response.strip()

            # Parse the JSON
            data = json.loads(json_str)

            # Validate required fields
            required_fields = ["response_text", "response_type", "confidence"]
            for field in required_fields:
                if field not in data:
                    raise ValueError(f"Missing required field: {field}")

            # Create ResponseSchema object
            return ResponseSchema(
                response_text=data["response_text"],
                response_type=data["response_type"],
                suggested_actions=data.get("suggested_actions", []),
                confidence=data["confidence"]
            )

        except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to parse Ollama response: {str(e)}")
            logger.error(f"Raw response: {response}")

            # Return default response on parsing failure
            return ResponseSchema(
                response_text="Thank you for contacting support. We have received your request and will get back to you shortly. If this is urgent, please contact our support team directly.",
                response_type="escalation",
                suggested_actions=["Contact support team", "Check status page"],
                confidence=0.5
            )

docs.title: process(task_context: TaskContext) -> TaskContext
docs.text:
Process the response generation workflow.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default task_context TaskContext

The task context containing ticket and classification data

required

Returns:

Type Description TaskContext

Updated TaskContext with generated response

Source code in app/workflows/customer_support_nodes/generate_response_node.py 
def process(self, task_context: TaskContext) -> TaskContext:
    """Process the response generation workflow.

    Args:
        task_context: The task context containing ticket and classification data

    Returns:
        Updated TaskContext with generated response
    """
    self.start_time = time.time()
    ticket = task_context.event

    logger.info(f"Starting response generation", extra={
        "ticket_id": ticket.id,
        "node": self.node_name,
        "status": "started"
    })

    try:
        # Get classification from previous node
        classification_node = task_context.nodes.get("ClassifyTicketNode", {})

        if classification_node.get("status") != "completed":
            raise ValueError("Classification node did not complete successfully")

        classification = classification_node.get("classification")

        # Build the response prompt using the template
        prompt = self._build_response_prompt(ticket, classification)

        # Call Ollama API
        response_result = self._call_ollama(prompt)

        # Parse the JSON response
        response_data = self._parse_ollama_response(response_result)

        # Calculate processing time
        processing_time = time.time() - self.start_time

        # Store results in task context
        task_context.nodes[self.node_name] = {
            "status": "completed",
            "response": response_data,
            "processing_time": processing_time,
            "model_used": self.model
        }

        logger.info(f"Response generation completed", extra={
            "ticket_id": ticket.id,
            "node": self.node_name,
            "status": "completed",
            "processing_time": processing_time,
            "response_type": response_data.response_type
        })

    except Exception as e:
        processing_time = time.time() - self.start_time if self.start_time else 0

        logger.error(f"Response generation failed", extra={
            "ticket_id": ticket.id,
            "node": self.node_name,
            "status": "error",
            "error": str(e),
            "processing_time": processing_time
        })

        task_context.nodes[self.node_name] = {
            "status": "error",
            "error": str(e),
            "processing_time": processing_time
        }

    return task_context

docs.title: Production Guide
docs.text: This guide describes how to run the Customer Support System in production with a focus on reliability, security, and operability while keeping the MVP simple.

docs.title: Architecture (MVP)
docs.text:
• API (FastAPI/Uvicorn)
  • Worker (Celery with Redis broker/result backend)
  • Database (PostgreSQL)
  • Local LLM (Ollama, e.g., llama3.1:8b)
  • Optional reverse proxy (Nginx/Caddy) for TLS, routing, and limits

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Postgres 15+ reachable from API and Worker
  • Redis 6+ reachable from API and Worker
  • Ollama running where the Worker can reach it
  • Pull model once: ollama pull llama3.1:8b
  • Serve: ollama serve (port 11434 by default)
  • A domain and TLS termination (e.g., Nginx/Caddy, or managed ingress)

docs.title: Required Environment Variables
docs.text:
Set these via your platform’s secret manager or a .env file (do not commit secrets):

# Project
PROJECT_NAME=customer_support_system

# Database
DATABASE_HOST=localhost
DATABASE_NAME=genai_launchpad
DATABASE_USER=postgres
DATABASE_PASSWORD=customer_support_password
DATABASE_PORT=5432

# Redis
REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/0

# Ollama
OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434
OLLAMA_MODEL=llama3.1:8b

# API
PORT=8080

# Worker
CELERY_WORKER_CONCURRENCY=1  # tune per CPU/RAM

docs.title: Database Migrations
docs.text:
• Migrations must run before first start and on every deploy:
  • Using provided script: ./scripts/migrate.sh
  • Or: cd app && PYTHONPATH=.. uv run alembic upgrade head
  • Ensure indexes exist for common queries (status, customer_email) — included in the migrations.
  • Backups: schedule pg_dump and verify restore regularly.

docs.title: Starting Services (Systemd example)
docs.text:
Below are minimalist systemd units for API and Worker. Adjust paths and users.

# /etc/systemd/system/customer-support-api.service
[Unit]
Description=Customer Support API
After=network.target

[Service]
WorkingDirectory=/srv/customer-support
EnvironmentFile=/srv/customer-support/.env
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/uv run uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port ${PORT}
Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

# /etc/systemd/system/customer-support-worker.service
[Unit]
Description=Customer Support Celery Worker
After=network.target

[Service]
WorkingDirectory=/srv/customer-support
EnvironmentFile=/srv/customer-support/.env
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/uv run celery -A app.worker.config.celery_app worker --loglevel=info -c ${CELERY_WORKER_CONCURRENCY}
Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

Reload and start:

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now customer-support-api customer-support-worker

docs.title: Reverse Proxy (Nginx)
docs.text:
Terminate TLS and proxy to API:

server {
  listen 443 ssl http2;
  server_name support.example.com;

  ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/support.example.com/fullchain.pem;
  ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/support.example.com/privkey.pem;

  client_max_body_size 2m;
  proxy_read_timeout 120s;

  location / {
    proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
  }
}

docs.title: CORS and UI
docs.text:
• The test UI is served at /ui by the API, ensuring same-origin and no CORS changes needed.
  • If hosting the UI separately, either proxy it under the same domain or add CORS in code for that origin.

docs.title: Logging and Monitoring
docs.text:
• Logs: use JSON-friendly logs and ship to your aggregator
  • Uvicorn logs to stdout; capture via your process manager
  • Celery logs to stdout; capture similarly
  • Health: expose /healthz and /readyz
  • Metrics: start with request latency, error rate, Celery queue depth, task duration

docs.title: Security Hardening
docs.text:
• Only expose the API over HTTPS behind a proxy
  • Keep Ollama bound to localhost or private network
  • Rotate secrets; do not use defaults in production
  • Rate-limit endpoints at the proxy
  • Sanitize logs (no PII beyond what’s necessary)

docs.title: Scalability & Tuning
docs.text:
• API: scale processes/replicas at the proxy level
  • Worker: set CELERY_WORKER_CONCURRENCY to match CPU/memory; consider multiple workers on a queue
  • Database: use connection pooling (SQLAlchemy default); monitor CPU/IO; add indexes if needed
  • Ollama: choose a model that fits memory; for low-RAM targets, consider phi3:mini as a drop-in

docs.title: Backup & Restore
docs.text:
# Backup
pg_dump -h $DATABASE_HOST -U $DATABASE_USER -d $DATABASE_NAME -Fc -f backup_$(date +%F).dump

# Restore
pg_restore -h $DATABASE_HOST -U $DATABASE_USER -d $DATABASE_NAME --clean backup_xxx.dump

docs.title: Deployment Checklist
docs.text:
• Application
  • [ ] .env created with production values
  • [ ] Alembic migrations applied
  • [ ] API and Worker started and healthy
  • [ ] /ui and /docs reachable (optional in prod)
  • Platform
  • [ ] TLS enabled on reverse proxy
  • [ ] Rate limiting and basic WAF rules applied
  • [ ] Centralized logging in place
  • Dependencies
  • [ ] Postgres reachable with correct creds
  • [ ] Redis reachable
  • [ ] Ollama running and model pulled

docs.title: CI/CD Essentials
docs.text:
• On every build: uv run ruff check, uv run ruff format --check, uv run pyright, pytest
  • On deploy: run Alembic migrations; restart API and Worker with zero-downtime strategy

docs.title: Smoke Test (Post-Deploy)
docs.text:
curl -f https://support.example.com/healthz
curl -f -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "id":"smoke_test",
  "customer_email":"ops@example.com",
  "subject":"Health check",
  "content":"Ping",
  "priority":"low"
}' https://support.example.com/support/tickets

docs.title: API returns 500 on ticket submission: relation does not exist
docs.text:
• Cause: migrations not applied
  • Fix: ./scripts/migrate.sh or start via ./scripts/start_all.sh

docs.title: API returns 500: password authentication failed for user "postgres"
docs.text:
• Cause: DATABASE_PASSWORD mismatch
  • Fix: export the correct password (defaults used in tests: customer_support_password) and restart API/worker

docs.title: Worker fails with Ollama timeouts
docs.text:
• Cause: first call cold start; heavy model; high concurrency
  • Fix: pull model, ensure ollama serve is running, use phi3:mini, set CELERY_WORKER_CONCURRENCY=1

docs.title: Docs show ModuleNotFoundError: app
docs.text:
• Cause: mkdocstrings cannot import project
  • Fix: run with PYTHONPATH=., or use ./scripts/start_docs.sh

docs.title: Cannot connect to DB
docs.text:
• Verify .env DATABASE_* values
  • Ensure Postgres is running and accessible

docs.title: Retry endpoint returns 404
docs.text: • Ticket ID not found; ensure it exists and is persisted (DB up and migrated)

docs.title: Worker does not start: "exec: PYTHONPATH=.: not found"
docs.text:
• Cause: shell exec syntax
  • Fix: use the provided scripts/start_worker.sh (exports PYTHONPATH before exec) or run the celery command directly

docs.title: AI & Ollama Integration
docs.text: This project uses a local LLM via Ollama. No cloud keys required.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
• Install Ollama (per official docs) and run ollama serve
  • Pull a model, e.g.: ollama pull phi3:mini (lighter) or ollama pull llama3.1:8b
  • Ensure .env contains OLLAMA_BASE_URL and OLLAMA_MODEL

docs.title: How nodes call Ollama
docs.text:
• AnalyzeTicketNode → extracts category, sentiment, urgency from ticket
  • GenerateResponseNode → produces a helpful response
  • Both use HTTP POST to OLLAMA_BASE_URL/api/generate
  • Retries with exponential backoff are applied to handle first-call slowness

docs.title: Prompting
docs.text:
• Templates live in app/prompts/
  • Use Jinja to insert ticket/context
  • Output should be valid JSON only; avoid extra commentary to ease parsing

docs.title: Common issues
docs.text:
• First call slow/timeout: expected warm-up; retries exist; try smaller model
  • JSON parse errors: ensure prompt enforces JSON-only outputs; add guard parsing
  • Memory limits: use phi3:mini or reduce concurrency (CELERY_WORKER_CONCURRENCY=1)

docs.title: Tuning tips
docs.text:
• Keep prompts concise and explicit
  • Prefer deterministic formatting over creative prose for machine parsing
  • Log raw responses (already implemented) to refine prompts

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• FastAPI for API and docs
  • Celery + Redis for async tasks
  • PostgreSQL via SQLAlchemy and Alembic
  • Ollama for local LLM calls

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• API: app/api/*, app/main.py
  • Workflow: app/core/workflow.py, app/workflows/*
  • Nodes: app/workflows/customer_support_nodes/*
  • DB: app/database/*
  • Worker: app/worker/*
  • Schemas: app/schemas/*
  • Prompts: app/prompts/*
  • UI: app/static/index.html

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
1. Client submits ticket to API
  2. API persists ticket to DB (status=open) and enqueues Celery task
  3. Worker runs workflow nodes (analyze → classify → generate)
  4. Worker updates ticket with results (status=resolved or failed)
  5. UI polls /support/tickets for updates

docs.title: Code Walkthrough
docs.text: This is a guided tour of the core modules and how they work together.

docs.title: Entry point: app/main.py
docs.text:
• Creates FastAPI app, registers routers, health endpoints
  • Serves UI at /ui and redirects / → /docs
  • Startup hook can warm up Ollama

docs.title: API layer: app/api/
docs.text:
• router.py: aggregates sub-routers and health endpoints
  • customer_support_endpoint.py:
  • Submit ticket: POST /support/tickets
  • List tickets: GET /support/tickets
  • Get ticket by id: GET /support/tickets/{ticket_id}
  • Retry processing: POST /support/tickets/{ticket_id}/retry

docs.title: Schemas: app/schemas/customer_support_schema.py
docs.text:
• Pydantic models for input/output validation
  • SupportTicketSchema, SimpleClassificationSchema, ResponseSchema

docs.title: Database: app/database/
docs.text:
• session.py: SQLAlchemy engine/session setup (uses env settings)
  • support_ticket.py: SQLAlchemy model (support_tickets table)
  • repository.py: GenericRepository with get, create, update, list, exists

docs.title: Alembic: app/alembic/
docs.text:
• env.py: configuration and metadata target for migrations
  • versions/*.py: migration scripts (e.g., create support_tickets)
  • Run via ./scripts/migrate.sh or auto-run in start scripts

docs.title: Worker & tasks: app/worker/
docs.text:
• config.py: Celery app and Redis config
  • tasks.py: background processing for tickets; calls workflow

docs.title: Core workflow engine: app/core/workflow.py
docs.text:
• Runs a sequence of Nodes with shared TaskContext
  • Accepts event as dict or Pydantic model for flexibility

docs.title: Customer support workflow: app/workflows/customer_support_workflow.py
docs.text:
• Declares node ordering and connections
  • Primary nodes live under app/workflows/customer_support_nodes/

docs.title: Nodes
docs.text:
• AnalyzeTicketNode: calls Ollama to extract category/sentiment/urgency
  • Retries with backoff; parses structured JSON from LLM output
  • ClassifyTicketNode: lightweight rule-based or direct pass-through
  • GenerateResponseNode: calls Ollama to produce response text

docs.title: Prompts: app/prompts/ and app/services/prompt_loader.py
docs.text:
• Simple Jinja templates to standardize system prompts
  • Tip: keep outputs JSON-only to ease parsing

docs.title: UI: app/static/index.html
docs.text:
• Minimal front-end to submit and monitor tickets
  • Filters, retry, error display, copy/download AI response

docs.title: Settings: app/core/config.py
docs.text: • Centralized env-based settings (DB, Redis, Ollama)

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
• Node-level logs indicate start/finish and status
  • Errors include context (e.g., raw Ollama text on parse failure)

Use this walkthrough while reading the code to speed up comprehension.

docs.title: Branching
docs.text:
• Feature branches: feature/<short-desc>
  • Fix branches: fix/<short-desc>

docs.title: Commits (Conventional)
docs.text:
• feat(api): add ticket submission endpoint
  • fix(db): apply pool_pre_ping

docs.title: Quality checks
docs.text:
• Lint/format: uv run ruff check --fix && uv run ruff format
  • Types: uv run pyright
  • Tests: uv run pytest

docs.title: PR checklist
docs.text:
• Description + rationale
  • How to test
  • No failing checks

docs.title: ORM & Models
docs.text:
• SQLAlchemy is used for models and sessions
  • Main model: SupportTicket in app/database/support_ticket.py

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
• Created in app/database/session.py with pool_pre_ping=True
  • Use the repository pattern (app/database/repository.py) inside API and worker

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
• Alembic configs in app/alembic/ (and app/alembic.ini)
  • Run migrations:
  • ./scripts/migrate.sh (default upgrade head)
  • or auto-run via ./scripts/start_api.sh / ./scripts/start_worker.sh

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• “relation support_tickets does not exist” → run migrations
  • Auth errors → verify .env DB creds; ensure Postgres is running
  • Stale connections → pool_pre_ping=True mitigates; restart services if needed

docs.title: Developer Guide (Intern Onboarding)
docs.text: This guide helps you get productive quickly, even if you’re new to FastAPI, Celery, SQLAlchemy/Alembic, and Ollama.

docs.title: What you’ll build
docs.text:
• Process support tickets: analyze → classify → generate AI response
  • Stack: FastAPI API, Celery worker, PostgreSQL, Redis, Ollama LLM, SQLAlchemy, Alembic

docs.title: 1) Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python managed by uv (already configured)
  • Docker (optional, for DB/Redis) or local Postgres/Redis
  • Ollama installed and model pulled: ollama pull phi3:mini (or llama3.1:8b)

docs.title: 2) Environment
docs.text:
• Create .env (no example committed) and set values for your machine
  • Important vars: DATABASE_*, REDIS_URL, OLLAMA_BASE_URL, OLLAMA_MODEL

Example .env for local dev:

PROJECT_NAME=customer_support_system

DATABASE_HOST=localhost

REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0

OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434
OLLAMA_MODEL=llama3.1:8b

PORT=8080
CELERY_WORKER_CONCURRENCY=1

docs.title: 3) One‑click scripts
docs.text:
• Start all: ./scripts/start_all.sh
  • Runs migrations, starts API + Docs in background, Worker in foreground
  • Start API only: PORT=8080 ./scripts/start_api.sh
  • Start Worker only: CELERY_WORKER_CONCURRENCY=1 ./scripts/start_worker.sh
  • Start Docs only: DOCS_ADDR=127.0.0.1:9000 ./scripts/start_docs.sh
  • Stop all: ./scripts/stop_all.sh
  • Migrations: ./scripts/migrate.sh (defaults to upgrade head)

docs.title: 4) Where to look in the code
docs.text:
• API: app/api/ (routes) and app/main.py (app startup, health)
  • Workflows: app/workflows/customer_support_* and app/core/workflow.py
  • Nodes: app/workflows/customer_support_nodes/ (Analyze, Classify, Generate)
  • Database: app/database/ (models, session, repository)
  • Schemas: app/schemas/ (Pydantic request/response models)
  • Worker: app/worker/ (Celery config and tasks)
  • Prompts: app/prompts/ (prompt templates via Jinja2)
  • Settings: app/core/config.py (centralized env-based config)
  • UI: app/static/index.html (simple test console)

docs.title: 5) Typical dev flow
docs.text:
1. Run ./scripts/start_all.sh
  2. Open API docs: http://127.0.0.1:8080/docs
  3. Open UI: http://127.0.0.1:8080/ui
  4. Submit a ticket from the UI, watch worker logs for processing

docs.title: 6) Testing & Quality
docs.text:
• Run tests: uv run pytest
  • Lint/format: uv run ruff check --fix && uv run ruff format
  • Types: uv run pyright

Pre-commit (optional): configure hooks to run ruff and pytest -q before commits.

docs.title: 7) Common pitfalls (quick)
docs.text:
• “relation support_tickets does not exist”: run migrations or use start scripts
  • Ollama timeout on first call: expected; retries/backoff are in place; ensure model is pulled
  • Auth/connection errors: ensure .env is loaded, DB/Redis running

If API starts but submit fails with 500: check /tmp/api.out and verify DB/Redis/Ollama reachability.

docs.title: 8) What to change first
docs.text:
• Prompts under app/prompts/ to tune AI outputs
  • Node logic in AnalyzeTicketNode and GenerateResponseNode
  • Simple classification thresholds or mapping in ClassifyTicketNode

You’re ready to contribute. For deeper explanations, see the other Development pages.

docs.title: Glossary (Quick Reference)
docs.text:
• FastAPI: Python web framework for APIs
  • Celery: background task queue
  • Redis: broker/result backend for Celery
  • SQLAlchemy: ORM for database models and queries
  • Alembic: migration tool for SQLAlchemy
  • Pydantic: data validation models
  • Ollama: local LLM server (no cloud dependency)
  • Uvicorn: ASGI server for FastAPI
  • Repository Pattern: abstraction layer for DB CRUD
  • Workflow/Node: pipeline stages executed in sequence
  • TaskContext: shared state passed between nodes

docs.title: Unit / Integration
docs.text:
• Install dev deps: uv sync
  • Run tests: uv run pytest -q
  • Mark long-running tests as @pytest.mark.integration and deselect with -m "not integration".

docs.title: What is covered
docs.text:
• Health endpoints
  • Prompt loading
  • Workflow with mocked Ollama
  • Legacy workflow script tests

docs.title: Writing new tests
docs.text:
• Unit: isolate node logic; mock network/DB calls
  • Integration: use FastAPI TestClient; run Celery worker if testing async flow
  • Prefer asserts over prints/returns; keep tests small and focused

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The app reads settings from environment variables. Key variables:

  • DATABASE_HOST, DATABASE_NAME, DATABASE_USER, DATABASE_PASSWORD, DATABASE_PORT
  • REDIS_URL (e.g., redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0)
  • OLLAMA_BASE_URL (default: http://localhost:11434)
  • OLLAMA_MODEL (default: llama3.1:8b)

All values are centralized in app/core/config.py.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12+
  • uv (python package manager)
  • Docker Desktop (Postgres & Redis), or local services
  • Ollama with llama3.1:8b

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
uv sync
# Start services (Postgres, Redis, Ollama)
cd app && PYTHONPATH="$(dirname "$PWD")" uv run alembic upgrade head && cd ..
DATABASE_HOST=localhost DATABASE_NAME=genai_launchpad DATABASE_USER=postgres \
DATABASE_PASSWORD=customer_support_password DATABASE_PORT=5432 \
OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434 REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0 \
uv run uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Install
uv sync

# Run migrations
cd app && PYTHONPATH="$(dirname "$PWD")" uv run alembic upgrade head && cd ..

# Start API
DATABASE_HOST=localhost DATABASE_NAME=genai_launchpad DATABASE_USER=postgres \
DATABASE_PASSWORD=customer_support_password DATABASE_PORT=5432 \
OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434 REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0 \
uv run uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080

# Submit a ticket
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/support/tickets" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"id":"test1","customer_email":"user@example.com","subject":"Login","content":"Cannot login","priority":"high"}'

docs.title: Where to go
docs.text:
• Web app: http://localhost:8080/ui
  • Help site: http://127.0.0.1:9000

docs.title: Submit a ticket
docs.text:
1. Open the web app
  2. Enter Email, Subject, Message, and Priority
  3. Click Submit – the ticket appears in the list
  4. The list auto-refreshes every 10 seconds; you can also click Refresh

docs.title: See the response
docs.text:
• A background worker processes your ticket and generates an AI response
  • The ticket card shows Status, Category, Sentiment, Urgency, and AI Response
  • If an error occurs, it will show under the ticket card

docs.title: If responses don’t show
docs.text:
• Ensure the worker is running
  • The first run of the AI model can take some time to warm up
  • Submit again after a minute if needed

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: • This runs locally; your data stays on your machine
